claims.claim: Evagrius Ponticus was a fourth‑century Christian monk, deacon and former lector who was born in Ibora in Pontus around 345 AD and died in the Egyptian desert at Scetis in 399 AD.
The Gnostikos (Greek Γνωστικός, “The Gnostic”) is a brief treatise of fifty chapters written by Evagrius Ponticus in the fourth century.
Evagrius wrote the Gnostikos to give counsel and spiritual instruction to experienced monks who had attained the status of “gnostic” – those worthy of higher knowledge.
The treatise emphasizes monastic pedagogy, using esoteric teachings and biblical symbolism to train monks in the acquisition of spiritual knowledge.
Although Evagrius was later condemned for Origenist views, the Gnostikos was preserved because the Armenian and Syriac churches continued to cherish his writings.
The original Greek text of the Gnostikos is largely lost; it survives only in a complete Syriac translation, an Armenian version, and in fragmentary Greek quotations preserved in later compilations.
